referencePolicy.stateExamples: Loading, empty, error, conflict, and confirmation examples describe possible runtime states. They are not an instruction to render those states together or to create separate static components.

modeStrategy.model: Manage and Normal are visibility modes of one shared surface.
modeStrategy.manage: Show host controls and operational details when the user has manage permission.
modeStrategy.normal: Reuse the same surface and hide host-only controls and operational details when the user lacks manage permission.
modeStrategy.referenceCoverage: Most references capture Manage mode. Bracket captures Normal mode as a clean read-only example. A second generated image is not required for every mode.

notes: Mobile references are the Issue #135 deliverable.
Desktop companions support the approved desktop-reference requirement in Issue #125.

Manage and Normal are visibility modes of one shared surface. Normal hides host-only controls and operational details; Manage shows them when the user has permission. Most references capture Manage, while Bracket captures Normal.
Manage Schedule view uses day-specific time ranges instead of a visible-hour slider. Breaks and greyed unavailable resource ranges show where a match cannot be moved.
All references use one shared six-tab shell. They remain draft assets outside the canonical directory.
The generated replacements use the current 8 px rectangular radius and BracketIQ navy, orange, and teal design.
Mobile references wrap the six tabs into two rows to keep every label visible.
The schedule shows an available Court 3 drop target at 11:00 AM. Grey hatched Resource ranges remain unavailable.
Loading, empty, error, conflict, and confirmation examples are separate reference states, not live components. Render only the state selected by current data, request outcome, and user action.
This replacement set remains unapproved. The existing commerce references for Issue #126 remain separate.
The supplemental set adds nine desktop and mobile pairs for nested workflows. It preserves the original 12 tab references.
The mobile match editor shows the upper form and a complete footer. Rules and bracket fields remain available through scrolling, as shown in the desktop reference.
Match incident and roster dialogs can open from Schedule. The shared bill dialog can open from Participants or Finance.
Team check-in is a saved status reference. The current captain confirmation flow remains in place. This reference does not add a host check-in action.
Event editing and rental checkout reuse the shared form and commerce references listed in surface-coverage.md.
